A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same L2T research work. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original pre-training experiments with 500M and 1B models, BLiMP and general-benchmark results, individual-task ablations, and mixing-ratio analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports psychometric evaluations and six additional SuperGLUE task results.

M1.justification: The same 14 language-learning transformations, raw/L2T data construction, Qwen2.5-based models, and all-token causal-language-modeling objective are retained. Section 2 and Appendix B do not introduce or revise a method component.

E1.justification: v2 substantially broadens evaluation through numerical distance/ratio effects, conceptual understanding, and Raven Progressive Matrices (Table 4), plus BoolQ, CB, MultiRC, RTE, WiC, and WSC (Table 7). The English FineWeb-Edu training corpus and original linguistic and general benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Raw remains the comparator for the main experiments and the added evaluations. The individual-task and mixture comparators are also retained. The discussion proposes a future supervised-augmentation comparison but reports no such evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The added evaluations specify R-squared for numerical abilities, Spearman rho for latent-representation and zero-shot conceptual measures, RPM accuracy, and SuperGLUE accuracy except CB F1. Existing training budgets, model configurations, BLiMP scoring, and general-benchmark prompting settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The individual-task ablations, mixing-ratio study, and qualitative linguistic cases already appear in v1 Appendices D–F and are retained in v2 Section 5 and Appendices E–G. The relocated ablation plot preserves its results; the new benchmark tables do not introduce an ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: v1 specifies a single deterministic evaluation run. v2 additionally discloses one training run per configuration in the new Single Seed limitation. This is newly reported run information, with no additional runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests established.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 2–3 and the matched ablation and mixing-ratio figures retain their results. v2 adds substantial result sets in Tables 4 and 7, including 500M Disjoint RPM scores of 0.312 for Raw versus 0.366 for L2T, and BoolQ scores of 53.1 versus 40.6. These newly reported evaluations show both gains and losses.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical setup and task definitions are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2's additional evaluation metrics do not introduce mathematical derivations or formal properties.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the claims that L2T improves linguistic competence, accelerates its acquisition, and maintains competitive general performance. The introductory 11.3% and 2.8% improvement figures are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 substantially extends interpretation to abstract-pattern induction, human-like magnitude processing, and semantic categorization in Section 5. Appendix D applies the structural-versus-factual learning explanation to mixed SuperGLUE outcomes. New discussion also addresses single-seed reliability and the missing direct comparison with supervised augmentation.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix D explicitly states that single-task datasets originate from the reference datasets' source pool and are subsampled to exactly 25B tokens. v2 omits this footnote while retaining the 25B budget. General hyperparameters, software versions, hardware, training costs, and code/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang et al. (2019) for SuperGLUE and extends its use of Shah et al. (2024) to psychometric assessment. Appendix A's research positioning is retained. Updates to references such as FlashAttention-2 and Isambard-AI concern the same works.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Analysis section, moves and condenses the existing individual-task discussion into the main text, expands Limitations, and updates the appendix organization. Editing and restructuring are concentrated in these areas; most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 7, moves v1 Figure 4 into the main text as Figure 3, and redraws it with a shorter aspect ratio and adjusted typography. Several existing tables and plots are enlarged, and the task overview becomes Figure 4. The overall two-column design is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves assessment of L2T's strengths and limits through additional cognitive and NLU evidence, more accessible ablations, and disclosure of single-run training. Benefits are tempered by sparse details for the new evaluations, the lost sampling note, and overgeneralized interpretations. For example, Appendix D describes Disjoint CB declines although Table 7 reports 1B CB F1 of 21.3 for Raw and 33.6 for L2T. The central method and original results remain stable.
